_doc: Culinary -> USDA NASS crosswalk: Cost Index ingredient slugs -> NASS QuickStats commodity_desc (+ class_desc where NASS splits a commodity). The DESCRIPTIVE domestic-supply layer — US production volume + value, farm PRICE RECEIVED (farm-gate, a distinct point in the chain, NEVER the wholesale reference), acres, yield — paired with the Census import stream to give an honest IMPORT-RELIANCE read (share of US supply, by value, that is imported). NASS is US-gov public-domain, redistributable. Farm price is NOT the measured price tier and NOT a pressure driver — a separate descriptive layer (ADR-013 relaxation, descriptive-tier only). Every value is descriptive of the tracked record, never a forecast. The builder reads the raw national annual SURVEY rows (data/nass-domestic.jsonl) and selects the clean series per ingredient (fresh-market production, marketing-year farm price, area, yield); domain=TOTAL, source=SURVEY.
_fields: Per slug: commodity (NASS commodity_desc), optional class (class_desc filter where NASS splits — e.g. LETTUCE HEAD/ROMAINE/LEAF, ONIONS DRY, TOMATOES FRESH MARKET), optional note. Multiple slugs may share a commodity (all beef cuts -> CATTLE; NASS is live-animal / whole-commodity, not by retail cut).

tomato.note: Fresh-market tomatoes; NASS does not split cherry/roma/round at the survey level.

cherry-tomato.note: Shares the fresh-market tomato commodity; no cherry split in NASS.

iceberg-lettuce.note: NASS splits lettuce by class: head lettuce = iceberg-type.

butter-lettuce.note: Butterhead falls in NASS leaf/other lettuce.

red-onion.note: NASS dry onions not split by color.

green-onion.note: Green (spring) onions if NASS carries the class; else falls to dry onions.

russet-potato.note: NASS potatoes not split by variety at the national fresh series.

bell-pepper.note: NASS peppers; bell vs chili class where available.

napa-cabbage.note: Chinese/napa cabbage folds into NASS cabbage or greens.

shiitake.note: Specialty mushrooms fold into the NASS mushroom commodity.

zucchini.note: NASS squash not split by type.

kale.note: Kale falls in the NASS greens commodity.

pineapple.note: US pineapple is Hawaii/PR; small domestic share.

banana.note: US bananas are Hawaii/PR only — a tiny domestic share vs imports (expect very high import reliance).

lime.note: US lime production is negligible — expect near-total import reliance.

mango.note: US mango is Hawaii/PR/FL — tiny; expect high import reliance.

basil.note: Herb — NASS covers where Census imports could not; may be census-of-ag (5-yr) not annual survey.

ribeye.note: NASS is live cattle / total beef, not by retail cut — all beef cuts share the CATTLE commodity for the domestic production + farm-gate price layer.

pork-belly.note: NASS is live hogs, not by cut — all pork cuts share HOGS.

lamb.note: Sheep/lamb; NASS LAMB & MUTTON for product where present.

butter.note: NASS dairy-product series where present; else MILK farm price is the upstream.

catfish.note: US farmed catfish (aquaculture) — the one seafood NASS covers well; wild-caught US landings come from NOAA Fisheries.

tilapia.note: US farmed tilapia if NASS carries it; small vs imports.

_deliberately_absent: Most seafood/shellfish (wild-caught — comes from NOAA Fisheries, the next source, not NASS); imported-only pantry/spices with no US production (cashew, coconut, saffron, vanilla, cinnamon, cumin, turmeric, cloves, nutmeg, cardamom, black pepper, coffee, tea, canned goods, sauces); the Latin/specialty produce with no US survey series (tomatillo, chayote, jicama, nopales, cassava, yam, plantain — largely imported). Absence is honest: no US production layer where the US does not commercially grow the item.
_status: AUTHORED (crosswalk ready); the raw pull (data/nass-domestic.jsonl) is pending the operator's NASS_KEY fetch. Builder reads it forward-compatibly — NASS fields appear only once the data lands.
